Twelve of the fourteen edge ends stay within a team, 0.43 in each diagonal cell (accent); the single cross edge C–D puts 0.07 in each off-diagonal cell." width="100%"} The counts of `attribute_mixing_dict()` as a matrix: entry `[i][j]` is the fraction (or count) of edge ends joining a node with the `i`-th value to a node with the `j`-th value. A heavy diagonal means homophily; the nominal assortativity coefficient (`assortativity_nominal()`) is computed from exactly this matrix. NetworkX's `attribute_mixing_matrix()` returns only the matrix, ordered arbitrarily unless a `mapping=` is given. EdgeCase returns the matrix together with the attribute values labelling its rows and columns, sorted. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [attribute]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Name of the node attribute. Every node must have a value. [normalized]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), entries sum to `1`. If `False`, they are counts. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [tuple[list[list[float]], list]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `(matrix, values)`: the square matrix as a list of rows, and the attribute values labelling rows and columns, sorted (by their text if values are not comparable). ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If some node has no value for the attribute. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Mostly within-team ties put most of the weight on the diagonal: ::: {#9c29bdca .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("C", "D"), ("B", "C")]) ) graph.set_node_attrs("team", {1: "red", 2: "red", 3: "blue", 4: "blue"}) matrix, teams = graph.attribute_mixing_matrix("team") teams, [[round(v, 3) for v in row] for row in matrix] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (['blue', 'red'], [[0.333, 0.167], [0.167, 0.333]]) ``` ::: :::
